title: Foreign orbiters verify the terrain
verdict: CONFIRMED REAL TERRAIN - backdrop claim falsified. Skylines in two 1971 Apollo 15 surface photographs match the horizon computed from JAXA's 2008 Kaguya/SELENE Terrain Camera DEM to ~0.2 deg RMS, with unique best-fit azimuths exactly at the documented viewing directions.
headline: The 2008 Japanese Kaguya DEM reproduces the 1971 Apollo 15 skylines to 0.18-0.21 deg RMS (r = 0.998 / 0.995): AS15-88-11866 locks onto Mons Hadley Delta at azimuth 184.8 deg and AS15-86-11603 onto Mons Hadley at 46.3 deg - both exactly where the mission record says the cameras pointed, on mountains the DEM shows are 17-20 km away and 3.5-4.1 km high.
impressive: results/overlay_AS15-88-11866.png - the famous flag-salute photograph with the skyline predicted from the 2008 Japanese orbiter DEM drawn over it: the green curve rides the photographed ridge of Mons Hadley Delta across the whole frame (RMS 0.179 deg, r = 0.9985), passing behind the LM and reappearing on the low ridge beyond the Rover.

details.method: photo skyline pixels -> 3D rays (focal 61.1 mm calibrated, pixel scale from the film's 10 mm reseau grid = 75.2 px/mm); fit only camera yaw/pitch/roll by minimizing RMS vs the DEM-rendered 360-deg horizon (curvature drop d^2/2R included, R = 1737.4 km)
